note: Steps are short paraphrases of the linked public sources (fetched 2026-10-09), not medical advice. UK sources say 999; the app shows 911, the Philippine emergency hotline. 'Life Off Desk app guidance' cards describe app features only. Founder review recommended before release.

cards.title: Cuts and bleeding
steps: Wash and dry your hands; wear disposable gloves if you have them.
Press on the wound with a bandage or clean folded cloth.
If something is stuck in it, leave it in and press firmly on either side.
Raise an injured arm above head level; for a leg, lie down and raise it above the heart.
If blood soaks through, add another pad on top and keep pressing.
Every 10 minutes check the bandage isn't too tight.
callNow: The bleeding won't stop
Bright red blood spurts out
Numbness near the wound or trouble moving it
A very large or deep wound, or one on the face or palm
An object like glass is stuck in it

cards.title: Burns and scalds
steps: Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
No tap? Use cool bottled water or a wet towel.
Remove clothing or jewellery near the burn, but not anything stuck to it.
Once cooled, lay cling film loosely over it; don't wrap it around.
Don't use creams, oil, butter, plasters or sticky dressings; don't burst blisters.
callNow: The burn is very large or deep
It is on the face, genitals or bottom
It was caused by acid, chemicals or electricity

cards.title: Sprains and twisted ankles
steps: Protect: support the injury, for example with supportive shoes.
Rest: stop and avoid putting weight on it.
Ice: a wrapped ice pack for up to 20 minutes, every 2–3 hours.
Compression: wrap a bandage around it for support during the day.
Elevate: keep it raised on a pillow as much as possible.
For the first couple of days avoid heat, alcohol and massage.
callNow: You heard a crack when it happened
The limb looks misshapen or at an odd angle
It is numb or tingling
The skin is blue, grey or cold

cards.title: Heat exhaustion and heatstroke
steps: Move the person somewhere cool.
Remove unnecessary clothing like jackets or socks.
Give plenty of water; a sports drink or oral rehydration solution also helps.
Spray or sponge with cool water and fan them; put wrapped cold packs on armpits or neck.
Stay with them; they should feel better within 30 minutes.
If unconscious, use the recovery position; give CPR if there are no signs of life.
callNow: Still unwell after 30 minutes of cooling and fluids
Hot skin that isn't sweating
Fast heartbeat or fast breathing
Confusion or poor coordination
A seizure or loss of consciousness

cards.title: Fainting and feeling faint
steps: Feeling faint? Lie down with legs raised, or sit with your head between your knees.
Drink some water; cross your legs, rock on your toes or clench your fists.
If someone faints, gently shake their shoulders and ask loudly if they're OK.
No response: shout for help, tilt the head back and lift the chin.
Check breathing for 10 seconds; if normal, lay them on their back with legs raised.
Most people wake within 30 seconds.
callNow: They are not breathing
They can't be woken within 1 minute
Trouble speaking or moving, chest pain or palpitations
A seizure, a serious injury, or fainting while exercising or lying down

cards.title: Choking (adult)
steps: Ask "are you choking?" If they can breathe, speak or cough, let them cough.
Remove any obvious blockage from the mouth.
If coughing fails, lean them forward and give five sharp back blows between the shoulder blades.
Check the mouth after each back blow.
Still blocked: stand behind, fist between belly button and chest, pull sharply in and up, up to five times.
Keep repeating five back blows and five thrusts until help arrives.
callNow: The blockage hasn't cleared after back blows and thrusts
They become unresponsive (start CPR)

cards.title: CPR (adult, not breathing)
steps: Make sure it's safe; shake their shoulders and ask loudly "are you OK?"
No response: shout for help, tilt the head back, check normal breathing for up to 10 seconds.
Not breathing normally: have someone call 911 on speaker and find a defibrillator.
Heel of your hand mid-chest, other hand on top, arms straight, press down 5–6 cm.
Push 100–120 times a minute. Not trained? Keep giving continuous chest compressions.
Continue until help takes over, they breathe normally, or you are exhausted.
callNow: An adult is unresponsive and not breathing normally (occasional gasps are not normal breathing)
cards.sourceTitle: How to do CPR | St John Ambulance

cards.title: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)
steps: Use an adrenaline auto-injector (e.g. EpiPen) if there is one; instructions are on the side.
Call 911 and say you think it's anaphylaxis.
Lie down with legs raised; if breathing is hard, sit up slowly.
If stung, remove the sting if it's still in the skin.
No improvement after 5 minutes: use a second auto-injector.
Never stand or walk, even if feeling better.
callNow: Lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell
Breathing is fast or a struggle, or the throat feels tight
Skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale
Sudden confusion, drowsiness, or fainting

cards.title: Dog or cat bite or scratch (rabies risk)
steps: Wash the wound right away with soap or detergent.
Flush it with plenty of water for about 15 minutes.
Then apply an iodine-containing or antiviral antiseptic if you have one.
Don't put chili, plant juices, acids or alkalis on it.
Go to a health facility for assessment and rabies treatment; don't wait.
If it's safe, keep the animal confined and watch it for 10 days.
callNow: Any bite or scratch from an animal that could have rabies: get medical care today
A large or deep wound, or bleeding that won't stop

cards.title: Dehydration
steps: Drink fluids if you are thirsty, dizzy, tired, or your pee is dark.
If you feel sick, start with small sips and slowly drink more.
Avoid caffeine and alcohol.
With vomiting or diarrhoea, use oral rehydration solution.
Drink more in hot weather or when exercising; aim for pale pee.
callNow: Blue, grey, pale or blotchy skin, lips or tongue, or cold skin
Difficulty breathing or rapid breaths
Confusion, or being unusually sleepy or hard to wake

cards.title: Insect and bee stings
steps: Scrape the stinger out sideways with a fingernail or card edge.
Don't use tweezers; squeezing can push in more venom.
Wash the area with soap and water.
Hold a wrapped ice pack or cold wet cloth on it for at least 20 minutes; raise it.
Don't scratch.
callNow: Stung in the mouth, throat or near the eyes
Stung many times, or a serious reaction before
Any sign of anaphylaxis: swelling of lips or throat, trouble breathing

cards.title: Snake bite
steps: Treat every snake bite as an emergency: call 911 or go to a hospital.
Stay calm and keep the bitten part as still as possible.
Remove jewellery and loosen clothing near the bite.
Remember the snake's colour and pattern, or photograph it from a safe distance.
Don't catch or kill the snake, suck or cut the bite, or tie anything tight around it.
callNow: Any snake bite
cards.sourceTitle: Snake bites - NHS (UK page; outside the UK use local emergency services)

cards.title: Wild plants, berries and mushrooms
steps: This app cannot identify plants or mushrooms, and a description is not enough to know one is safe.
Some plants and mushrooms are poisonous; if someone may have eaten one, call 911 or go to a hospital.
Don't make them vomit, and don't give them anything to eat or drink.
Keep a sample of what was eaten to show the doctors.
If unconscious but breathing, use the recovery position; if not breathing, start CPR.
callNow: Something harmful may have been eaten (symptoms can take hours or days)
Unconscious, not breathing, or breathing is very difficult
A seizure

cards.title: Floods (baha)
steps: Don't walk or drive through flooded areas or standing water.
Hidden dangers include fallen power lines and chemicals; currents can sweep people away.
Know your community's evacuation route and flood-prone areas.
Wash hands with soap after touching floodwater; never use it for food, dishes or teeth.
Throw away food that touched floodwater; boil or chlorinate drinking water.
callNow: Someone is trapped or swept away by water
Live wires are down in or near the water
cards.sourceTitle: Floods: How to protect your health - WHO

cards.title: Lightning and thunderstorms
steps: When thunder roars, go indoors: hearing thunder means you're within striking distance.
Only an enclosed building or a car is safe; tents and open shelters are not.
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back outside.
If stuck outside, avoid open fields, hilltops and tall isolated trees.
Groups should spread out; stay away from water and metal fences or poles.
cards.sourceTitle: Lightning Safety - US National Weather Service

cards.title: Feeling unsafe, followed or threatened
steps: If you are in danger now, call 911.
Go towards people and lit, busy places such as a store, guard post or police station.
In this Help screen, the nearest police stations have a Route button (offline).
Copy or text your location from this screen to someone you trust (SMS works without data).
callNow: You or someone else is in immediate danger
cards.sourceTitle: Life Off Desk app guidance (not medical)

cards.title: Lost or not sure where you are
steps: Stay calm and stop walking for a moment.
Tap Locate on the map; your position works offline while GPS has a fix.
Copy or text your location from this Help screen to someone you trust.
Pick a place on the map and follow the dashed suggested route along mapped streets.
callNow: You are hurt, in danger, or it is getting dark somewhere unsafe
cards.sourceTitle: Life Off Desk app guidance (not medical)

cards.title: Phone battery running low
steps: Turn on Low Power Mode: Settings › Battery (or Control Center, battery icon).
Low Power Mode dims the screen and pauses background tasks to save battery.
With no signal, Airplane Mode stops the phone searching for a network, which drains battery.
Before it runs out, text your location to someone you trust.
cards.sourceTitle: Use Low Power Mode to save battery life on your iPhone - Apple Support

cards.title: Location not updating
steps: This app works without data; GPS itself needs no signal or internet.
If the app says "Finding your location…", move to an open area away from tall buildings and wait a moment.
Check Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services is on for Life Off Desk.
Your last saved adventure and the map still work while the location catches up.
cards.sourceTitle: Life Off Desk app guidance (not medical)
